culturalBackground: In South Asian and many Arab weddings, the bride's feet are decorated with henna along with her hands.
The soles of the feet, like the palms, have thick skin and take a very dark stain.
Common layouts include an anklet-style band, a trail from the toes to the ankle, and a mandala on the top of the foot.
The top of the foot stains lighter than the sole because the skin there is thinner.
applicationTips: Sit with the foot supported on a stool so you can keep still for the whole application.
Do not walk until the paste is fully dry; keep slippers and a towel within reach before you start.
Exfoliate the feet a day before, since dry skin sheds quickly and takes the stain with it.

faqPool.q: Does mehndi stain darker on feet?
faqPool.a: On the soles, yes. The thick skin there stains as dark as the palms. The top of the foot stains lighter.

faqPool.q: How long should foot mehndi dry before walking?
faqPool.a: Wait until the paste is completely dry, usually 30 to 45 minutes, and then walk carefully in open slippers.

faqPool.q: Is foot mehndi only for brides?
faqPool.a: No. Simple anklet-style and toe designs are popular for festivals and summer as well.
